messages:
Alex Palmer: Heads-up: I'm stepping off shift in 10m. Summary of current state: customer-facing API latency within SLO except a small tail for embeddings requests. No open pages from the incident bot right now.
Sara Liu: copying — thanks. Do you have any running mitigation or throttles active?
Alex Palmer: No active throttles. We left a temporary KV cache warming job running but it's low-priority. Key runbook refs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-tail and the ember config checklist: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/ember-cache.
Tony Morales: pinging in — I'll be primary for the next 4h. Sara, can you take secondary?
Sara Liu: I can take secondary. Tony, if pager goes to primary and you don't ack in 2m, incident-bot will escalate to secondary, correct?
incident-bot: Incident policy check: channel=eng-oncall, pager window=24/7, primary_ack_window=2m, secondary_escalation=automated. See /policies on the console.
Tony Morales: Correct. If primary misses ack, secondary gets the page automatically. If secondary doesn't ack within 3m, on-call rotation group page goes out.
Maria Khan: Quick Q — we saw a minor latency blip on embeddings at 07:12 UTC. Any correlation with batch jobs?
Alex Palmer: Blip at 07:12 coincides with a heavy prefix fill from the batch-runner. I throttled batch-runner locally at 07:15 which brought p95 back. Note in incident timeline.
Sara Liu: Noted. Can we add a short-lived rule to route embeddings through smaller model variant during high prefix load? That's in the Optimize playbook.
Tony Morales: Good idea. Short-term plan if we see repeat: 1) flip routing rule to embeddings-lite (canary) 2) add cache priming priority 3) notify support + status. Runbook snippet: 
```
# quick mitigation
route embeddings -> embeddings-lite
increase cache TTL for prefix keys to 120s
notify #support with impact template
```
Alex Palmer: For escalation: page SRE lead if customer impact > 10% error or > 2x latency SLO for > 5m. Page infra-eng if GPU pool contention suspected. Page product-manager only for active customer outages.
Sara Liu: Clarifying paging rules: do we page infra-eng directly or always go through SRE lead?
Tony Morales: Page SRE lead first unless you can clearly identify infra contention (OOMs, pod evictions, disk pressure). If infra is obvious from logs and metrics, page infra-eng and SRE lead concurrently.
Maria Khan: Where's the runbook pointer for the paging matrix?
Alex Palmer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paging-matrix — short cheat sheet in the header. I also left a sticky in the runbook about fallback contacts: slack handles and phone numbers (on the secure vault).
Sara Liu: For the handoff checklist: 
- confirm primary/secondary acknowledged (Tony/Sara)
- confirm runbook links in thread (done)
- outstanding mitigations documented (cache warm job)
- support updated if user-facing (not needed currently)
Alex Palmer: All done here. Leaving a quick note for whoever follows: if you see a creeping tail, immediately check KV hit-rate and the continuous-batcher queue depth (metrics: infra.kv.hitrate, runtime.batch.queue_depth). If those look bad, start the routing rule and notify infra.
Tony Morales: Got it. I'll ACK primary in 30s and monitor dashboards for 30m. Sara takes secondary. If anything, page me then incident-bot will escalate. :thumbsup:
Sara Liu: ACK secondary. Thanks Alex — enjoy your time off.
incident-bot: Handoff logged: previous_primary=Alex Palmer, new_primary=Tony Morales, new_secondary=Sara Liu, timestamp=1742500000. Handoff notes appended to rotation log.
Alex Palmer: leaving now. ping me if you need context.
Tony Morales: Thanks — monitoring now.
Sara Liu: closing handoff thread. If paged, follow escalation matrix and use runbook links above.
